summary: Iter 475 Employee Rejoin (Rehire) — FRONTEND ONLY testing. End-to-end flow verified on preview URL after fixing 2 blocker bugs in the freshly-added feature. Login (password), locate 'TEST REJOIN EMP' via /employee-master?user_id=user_test_rejoin1, click 'em-rejoin', /employee-rejoin loads with correct read-only previous card (Code 999 / LWD 2026-02-28 / resigned / UAN 100999888777), Service Summary shows Gap, Section B form fill (reason chip 'Business requirement', Designation 'SR HELPER', New Actual Salary 18000), submit -> 'Rejoined ✅' alert, navigation back. Re-opening the employee shows em-rejoin button GONE and Designation 'SR HELPER · PACKING' with Monthly Salary ₹18,000. No crash / blank screen. Both bugs FIXED IN PLACE by the testing agent (trivial mapping/serialization mistakes) and re-verified.

ui_bugs.issue: The gating block reads emp.exit_date / emp.resign_date / emp.employment_status / emp.active, but the Object.assign(e, {...}) that merges the /admin/employees list row into `emp` was NOT pass-throughing any of those four fields. Result: the green 'Rejoin Employee (Rehire)' button was NEVER rendered even for clearly separated employees (backend correctly returns resign_date='2026-02-28', employment_status='resigned', active=false for TEST REJOIN EMP). FIXED by adding active/employment_status/exit_date/resign_date to the Object.assign block around line 224.

Double JSON.stringify: submit() called api(`/admin/employees/${id}/rejoin`, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(body) }) but src/api/client.ts already does JSON.stringify(body) internally. Backend received a stringified JSON string and rejected with pydantic 422 model_attributes_type ('Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from') so EVERY submit failed with a red 'Rejoin failed' alert. FIXED by passing the raw object (body: body).

action_items: Review the two fixes I applied (employee-master.tsx Object.assign now spreads active/employment_status/exit_date/resign_date; employee-rejoin.tsx submit no longer double-stringifies) and keep them.
Consider adding a light regression guard: a shared helper on the employee list row → detail-panel mapping so future gating fields (like rehire/exit flags) can't silently be dropped.
Consider tightening the api client contract so passing a string body throws instead of getting silently double-serialized.
critical_code_review_comments: employee-master.tsx is 2325 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Splitting into smaller sub-components (identity, credentials, grouping, textile, OT, docs, rejoin) would have made the missing field mapping obvious.

The Rejoin gating logic is duplicated implicitly: backend `/admin/employees/{id}/rejoin-info` computes `eligible`, but the frontend reimplements the check from raw fields. Prefer fetching a lightweight `/eligible-for-rejoin` (or reusing rejoin-info.eligible via a cached call) so both stay in sync.

rca_of_issue: Bug 1 (RCA): The pattern in employee-master.tsx is: /admin/employees/{id}/policy gives base object → /admin/employees list is scanned for the same user_id → Object.assign whitelists specific fields into `emp`. When Iter 475 added the Rejoin gating that reads emp.employment_status/resign_date/exit_date/active, the developer forgot to whitelist those fields in the Object.assign, so they arrived as undefined and the Boolean(...) always evaluated to false. Reproduce: login as super_admin, open /employee-master?user_id=user_test_rejoin1 → button absent. Mitigation applied: added the four fields to the whitelist. Bug 2 (RCA): api client already JSON.stringify's body. employee-rejoin.tsx submit() also called JSON.stringify(body) so backend received `"{\"rejoin_date\":\"2026-08-03\",...}"` (a JSON-encoded string) instead of a dict, tripping FastAPI pydantic model_attributes_type validation. Every submit failed 422. Fix: pass raw object.
